predecessors.name: Kievan Rus'
predecessors.text: Polotsk, held by Iziaslav of Polotsk's line when Yaroslav's lands were divided (the rus dossier, Kievan Rus' page); Cliopatria's first Polotsk shape is 1056

successors.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
successors.text: Polotsk, a vassal of the Lithuanian princes from 1240 and annexed by Vytenis in 1307

ledger.x: 1054: Polotsk stands apart from the sons' division of Rus', the principality of the Vseslavichi's line.
1067: the Yaroslavichi sack Minsk and defeat Vseslav on the Nemiga.
1085: Cliopatria widens Polotsk to the west over Latgale and as far as Vilnius (+34,000 km2).
1101: Vseslav dies on 24 April and Polotsk is divided; Vitebsk goes to Sviatoslav Vseslavich.
1101: Jersika passes out of Polotsk's direct rule when the principality is divided after Vseslav's death.
1101: Koknese passes out of Polotsk's direct rule with the division after Vseslav's death.
1127: Mstislav of Kiev makes war on Polotsk.
1129: Mstislav annexes Polotsk and the contest ends in Kiev's favour.
1165: the princes of Smolensk take Vitebsk.
1168: Briachislav Vasilkovich recovers Vitebsk (the list: 'Briachislav Vasilkovich (1168-1175)'); 'Vitebsk later regained independence under Briachislav Vasilkovich.'
1186: Vitebsk falls again under Smolensk's influence.
1195: Polotsk and its allies restore Vitebsk.
1307: Vytenis of Lithuania annexes Polotsk by force.

wars.name: Nemiga campaign and Vseslav's captivity
wars.outcome: The Yaroslavichi sacked Minsk and beat Vseslav on the Nemiga (3 March 1067); he was imprisoned, freed by the Kiev uprising of 1068, held Kiev for about seven months and 'finally secured Polotsk in 1071'.

wars.name: Mstislav of Kiev's war on Polotsk
wars.outcome: Mstislav captured Vseslav's remaining sons in 1129 and exiled them to Constantinople; the Vitebsk page says he 'annexed Polotsk and its vassals including Vitebsk' (ledger loss 1129); the town invited Vasilko Sviatoslavich in 1132 (gain 1132) and the exiles…

wars.name: Smolensk's claims on Vitebsk
wars.outcome: Smolensk held Vitebsk in 1165-1168 and again had influence over it from 1186; Polotsk and Chernigov princes marched against Smolensk in 1195 and restored Vitebsk to Polotsk's rule.

wars.name: German crusade on the Daugava
wars.outcome: 'In 1209 German crusaders conquered the principalities of Jersika and Koknese'; in 1212 Polotsk was forced 'to permit free travel to German merchants'; in 1227 'Smolensk ceded Polotsk by treaty to the city of Riga' (infobox: vassal of the Livonian Brothers of…

wars.name: Lithuanian takeover of Polotsk
wars.outcome: Vassal of the Lithuanian princes from 1240; Tautvilas, Mindaugas's nephew, was given Polotsk in 1254 (Vitebsk page); annexed by force by Vytenis in 1307; autonomy to the 1390s.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened; the frontiers with Lithuanian, Latgalian and Livonian lands are approximate throughout.
